references.text: The recipe for the anointing oil is given here, with detailed instructions on the ingredients: myrrh, cinnamon bark, calamus, cassia, and olive oil.
The recipe for the fragrant incense for the sanctuary is described, with the ingredients stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense.
Oil for the lampstand and spices for the anointing oil and the fragrant incense are mentioned among the gifts the Israelites were to bring.
Oil for the lampstand, spices for the anointing oil and the fragrant incense are mentioned as offerings for the tabernacle.
The altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense are referred to as parts of the tabernacle's equipment.
Bezalel made the holy anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense according to the art of the perfumer, in accordance with God's command.
Moses is commanded to anoint the tabernacle and all its furnishings with the anointing oil to consecrate them.
Moses uses the anointing oil to anoint the tabernacle, the altar, and Aaron, fulfilling God's command.
The oil mentioned in 31:11 is the central means of consecration described in 40:9.
The general command in 31:11 is specified theologically and practically in the recipe given in 30:25.
The command regarding incense in 31:11 finds its concrete form of execution in 30:35.
The status of the oil as 'holy' in 31:11 is linked to its perpetual validity for all generations in 30:31.
The command in 31:11 is the basis for the 'most holy' status described in 30:29.
